input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?
I’m not very good with technical things, but I’ll try my best if you walk me through it slowly. What do you need me to do first?
I ran the check, and it says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?

I checked the network status, and here’s what it says:
- Airplane mode is ON
- SIM card status: missing
- Cellular connection: no service
- Signal: none
- Mobile data is enabled
- Data roaming is off
- Wi-Fi is off and not connected

What should I do with this information?

I turned off Airplane Mode, but it still says there’s no SIM card detected in the phone. I’m not sure what to do next—should I try taking the SIM card out and putting it back in? I get nervous about opening up my phone. Will I lose anything important, like my photos, if I do this?

I took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now it says:
- Airplane mode is off
- SIM card status: active
- Cellular connection: connected, but the signal is poor
- Network type: 2G
- Mobile data is enabled
- Data roaming is still off
- Wi-Fi is off

What should I do next? Will this help me send picture messages now?

I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and now it says:
- Cellular connection: connected
- Signal: excellent
- Network type: 5G
- Mobile data is enabled
- Data roaming is still off

Does this mean I can try sending a picture message again now, or is there something else I need to do?
I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet," but the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. Does that mean something is missing? What should I do next?

I’ve reset the APN settings, but it says the changes will take effect after I reboot my phone. I’m a bit nervous—if I restart my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? Can you reassure me before I do this?
I restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? Is there anything else we can try?

I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Also, my messaging app only has permission for the phone—it doesn’t seem to have permission for storage or anything else. Should I turn off Wi-Fi Calling or change the app permissions? Which one should I do first?
I’ve turned off Wi-Fi Calling. What should I do next about the messaging app permissions? Could you guide me through updating those?

I updated the permissions for the messaging app to include storage and SMS, and I restarted my phone again, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this will never work.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
